newsitem.title: CHINA: China to favor U.S., Europe in retail sector.
newsitem.headline: China to favor U.S., Europe in retail sector.

text.p: China said Saturday it would expand cooperation with foreigners in the nation's retail sector and that big companies from the United States and Europe would be given priority.
But the official China Daily newspaper said Beijing wanted to ensure that Chinese firms retained majority control in retail joint venture projects.

The newspaper quoted Huang Hai, director-general of the Ministry of Internal Trade's policy and regulation department, as saying that China would ease restrictions on the number and location of foreign-invested stores.
China has been gradually opening up its once-closed retail sector to foreign companies, though it still is concerned about competition with domestic companies.
The ministry also would set "appropriate cooperation terms" as part of its efforts to ensure smooth development of the sector, the newspaper said without elaborating.
"In selecting future partners, China will give priority to large European and U.S. companies whose major business is in the retail sector," the newspaper said.
The China Daily was referring to projects that required central government approval. Local governments have also cleared many joint ventures in the retail sector.
